articles.title: Greer Sees US Trade Probe Certainly Concluding by Year End
articles.summary: USTR Jamieson Greer expects to conclude a pending investigation into excess industrial capacity very soon, adding a potential source of tension ahead of a US-China trade truce expiration in January. Asked about timing in a Bloomberg Television interview, Greer said 'certainly' the process would be completed by year end. He declined to say which countries would face potential additional tariffs.

articles.title: EU tech chief says bloc well equipped to fend off rogue AI risk
articles.summary: EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen told Reuters that EU rules setting guardrails on AI use are more than capable of tackling rogue agents, following recent incidents at OpenAI and Anthropic. The AI Act, which regulates use based on risk level, is seen as the world's strictest AI rules. The Commission sent requests for information to more than 30 AI companies in late August; such requests can lead to investigations and fines of up to 7 percent of global annual turnover.

articles.title: AI Safety Framework Bill Teased by Bipartisan House Lawmakers
articles.summary: A bipartisan House trio outlined a sweeping new artificial intelligence proposal that would require companies to adhere to minimum federal safety standards and disclose any lapses while clarifying where liability lies for foreseeable injuries tied to the technology. The announcement previews a forthcoming bill led by Reps. Sara Jacobs, Don Beyer and Celeste Maloy, known as the SAFE AI Act.

articles.title: US AI Chip Crackdown Shakes Supply Chains
articles.summary: The US Commerce Department announced stricter export controls on AI chips, explicitly targeting data centers serving Chinese firms to close a loophole in prior restrictions. The move follows reports that nearly 880,000 AI chips were approved for export to China earlier this month. Nvidia confirmed it would halt sales of its most advanced chips to China, while Alibaba revised its cloud growth outlook downward citing the curbs as a direct constraint.

articles.title: Oil gains on Iran war worries and short-covering ahead of Thanksgiving holiday
articles.summary: Oil gained late in trading as worries about possible renewed attacks in the US-Israeli war with Iran and holiday short-covering lifted prices. Brent settled at 92.57 dollars a barrel, up 0.64 percent, while WTI finished at 83.98. Both benchmarks were on track for a third straight weekly decline as crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz returned to roughly pre-war levels. The Houthis warned of attacks on Saudi Red Sea ports and two tankers hit naval mines in the strait.

articles.title: Oil prices climb nearly 1 percent as Brent reaches 92.77 despite third straight weekly decline
articles.summary: Oil prices rose as renewed security concerns in Saudi Arabia and reported tanker incidents in the Strait of Hormuz revived fears over Middle East supply, although expectations of a wider crude surplus kept both benchmarks on course for a third consecutive weekly decline. Brent gained 0.9 percent to 92.77 dollars. US commercial crude inventories rose 3.4 million barrels in the week ending 13 November to 417.8 million barrels, adding pressure from surplus supply.

articles.title: Fed's Paulson calls for gradual rate hikes amid ongoing high inflation
articles.summary: Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson said the central bank has more interest rate increases ahead, and that further gradual tightening seems appropriate. She said monetary policy needs to be somewhat restrictive to bring inflation back to 2 percent, with underlying inflation pressures between 2.5 and 3 percent. She said inflation is being driven up by tariffs, energy prices and AI investment. Futures markets priced in strong odds of a quarter-point increase at the December 8-9 meeting.

articles.title: Oil Dependence Is Bad for the Climate and the Economy, UN Chief Tells COP31
articles.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres criticised fossil fuel dependency at COP31, saying nine oil companies are on track to rake in more than 95 billion dollars in just three months, more than one billion dollars a day, while families and governments pay the price. Host Turkey urged countries to sign a goal to increase electricity's share of global energy use to 35 percent by 2035, but climate advocates criticised the pledge because it does not require the additional electricity to be low-carbon.

articles.title: US inflation too high; essential to get back to 2%: Fed's Williams
articles.summary: US economic growth has remained resilient and the labour market remarkably stable despite successive shocks, but inflation is too high and must be brought back to 2 percent, New York Fed President John Williams said at a European Central Bank conference in Frankfurt. Inflation has soared globally, mostly as the US war on Iran pushed energy prices higher but also because soaring investment in AI has pushed up costs for some IT products and services. He said inflation expectations remain well anchored.
